stimulus.text:
In September 1786, commissioners from only five of the thirteen states — New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Virginia — met at Annapolis, Maryland, to discuss trade between the states. Their report said:
“Your Commissioners did not conceive it advisable to proceed on the business of their mission, under the Circumstance of so partial and defective a representation.”
— Report of the Commissioners to Remedy Defects of the Federal Government, Annapolis, September 14, 1786

options.text: the states had already fixed the trade problem
options.misconception: Background: the trade problem was unsolved, which is why the commissioners met at all.
Background: Congress had not forbidden the meeting; the commissioners simply lacked enough states.

the commissioners could not agree on where to meet
options.misconception: They met at Annapolis; the problem was how few states came, not where they met.

rationales.C: The report calls the representation partial and defective, and only five of the thirteen states — New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Virginia — had sent delegates.
rationales.A: Background: the trade problem was unsolved; that is why the commissioners met.
rationales.B: Background: Congress had not forbidden the meeting; the commissioners stopped because too few states came.
rationales.D: They did meet, at Annapolis; the problem was the thin attendance, not the place.
rationales.general:
1. Read the report's reason. The representation was partial and defective.
2. Only five of the thirteen states had sent delegates to Annapolis.
3. Five states could not settle trade rules for all thirteen, since the other eight had no voice in the room.
4. Background: the five were New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Virginia.
Remember: a meeting of five cannot speak for thirteen.
